9586d7ebe0e4939084e2dcf31bee882f00dda505.question: Which experiments tested flammability at high oxygen concentration?
9586d7ebe0e4939084e2dcf31bee882f00dda505.answer: SAFFIRE-II tested flammability at higher oxygen concentrations using multiple solid materials in a microgravity free-flying Cygnus vehicle [S1]. BASS-II extended tests to additional oxygen concentrations using solid fuels (fabrics and plastics) in microgravity aboard the International Space Station [S4]. Cool-flame transitions (ground) conducted ground-based experiments and numerical modeling using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to study oxygen concentration effects on extinction limits [S2]. The provided passages do not specify the exact oxygen concentration values used in these experiments.

c0a6bcdbbf805ec5e718dac34fc2e4b52d51459d.question: Can acrylic burn at 30 percent oxygen in microgravity?
c0a6bcdbbf805ec5e718dac34fc2e4b52d51459d.answer: Based on the provided passages, there is no microgravity flight evidence, ground evidence, or modelling evidence regarding whether acrylic can burn at 30 percent oxygen. The passages only provide evidence for acrylic burning at 17 percent oxygen [S1, S4] and polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) rods burning at oxygen concentrations ranging from 14 to 18 by volume [S3].

582068fd2a492be7c667fadab5111aa4cc2bc88c.question: Do cool flames matter for smoke detector choice?
582068fd2a492be7c667fadab5111aa4cc2bc88c.answer: No language model available, so this answer quotes the retrieved sources directly. The removal of buoyancy reduces the velocities in the high temperature zones in flames, increasing the residence time of smoke particles and consequently allowing longer growth time for the particles. [S1] Specific objectives were: (1) Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity.
